utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning. Who is the first witness today?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The first witness today is Ndrec Konaj, and we're calling him pursuant to 92 ter. His evidence pertains to paragraphs 72(e), 77, and 100 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Konaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you stand, please, for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Konaj, we have before us your statement, so we know a great deal about your evidence already, but you are going to be asked questions by a number of counsel to explain parts of the statement, perhaps to challenge parts of the statement, and also perhaps to add to it. The first counsel to question you will be for the Prosecutor and that will be Ms. Dragulev. Ms. Dragulev.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Konaj.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Could you please state your first name and your last name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Ndrec Konaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated the 12th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review this statement in Albanian during your proofing session last week?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And based on your review, did you make some minor corrections to the statement?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. One of those corrections was to page 2, paragraph 3 of your statement, where you refer to the change of the situation between the Serbian and Albanian neighbours as having occurred about 16 months ago. In the statement, it says it was the first Saturday in July 1998. At the time you gave the statement in June 2001, more than 16 months would have passed since July 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No. It's from 1998 that 16 months had passed. I made the -- when I made the changes, it was later.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you. And the other correction that you made was the reference to Salih Dreshaj. In the English version of your statement he's referred to as your best man; in the Albanian version he's referred to as your best friend. And in fact, he's your godfather. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Well, his son held my son's daughter on his arms, in his arms, and that's why we call him a godfather.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's deal with both of these. Is 1998 the correct date?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does that mean that this statement has been altered?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This was just a correction. The reference to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the one I have, which is the statement taken in June of 2001, has the date July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes, and that's a correct date, but there's a reference as to that date having occurred 16 months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And that reference is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's the 16 months we're concerned with.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. And the relationship we've just heard about sounds like maybe the godfather of his granddaughter. Is that what --

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you're really trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: I was just trying to point out that there was a minor correction; that this Salih Dreshaj is not the best man but the godfather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, godfather to the granddaughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, where is the reference to that in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: That is the second paragraph on the top of page 4 in the statement. The English ERN is K0203784.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Having made those two corrections, is your statement true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct and true. I said everything in the first one, and the second one is also correct, very correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you confirm to this Court that that evidence is what you would give under oath today if you were asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would like to tender Exhibit P2372, which is the statement dated the 12th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I would like to move to the events that occurred in Pec/Peje in March 1999. In your statement you said you saw two Pinzgauers at a gas station on that day; one was military and the other was police. Can you please describe the one that you identified as a military Pinzgauer. What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. And what colour was the military Pinzgauer?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Green, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And after that incident, you continued towards the bus station, and in your statement, you describe that at every side road there were three or four military or police. Could you please briefly describe the police. Did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Their own uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And what colour were those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: There were blue uniforms and also green uniforms. I don't know whether they were soldiers or paramilitaries; they had camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 28th of March, 1999, when you left the house of Salih Dreshaj to join the crowds, you state that there were police, army, and paramilitary troops located at the entrance of every street. Could you please briefly describe the police. Did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: There were police in uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And what colour were those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And could you please briefly describe the military. Did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: As I said earlier, they wore green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And the paramilitaries, did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: There were ones with green camouflage trousers, with black T-shirts, various kinds of clothes, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question, Mr. Konaj, relates to your return to Pec. When you returned to Pec, did you see any damaged houses?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Peje was one of the most destroyed towns as far as houses are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And did you see any damaged mosques or religious sites?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, there were damaged mosques as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Did you see any damaged churches?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The churches were not damaged because there were people sheltered in there, and the priests were there as well so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Konaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Dragulev. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll follow the indictment, and I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have no questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Konaj. My name is Djuro Cepic. I'm one of the Defence team of General Lazarevic. I would like to clarify a few points with you. I will try to ask short, clear, and concise questions, and I would appreciate answers of the same kind, preferably with a yes or a no. On the sixth page of the transcript today, you enumerated persons you encountered on the 24th of March. You said it was a group of about 30 persons, some wearing blue uniforms, whom you believed to be members of the MUP --

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the reference to the date is incorrect. It was not the 24th of March. I think it was the 27th of March, or the 28th --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, I said "28th." Probably it is a problem with interpretation. Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, may I continue, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as I said, you believed that members of the MUP, that is the police, had blue uniforms; members of the army, green uniforms; the paramilitaries wore various uniforms, and so on. The persons you encountered on that day were between 30 and 35 or 40 years of age. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I never said what their age was in my statement. There is no sentences in my statement about their age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you now for clarification.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly what age. About 30, I don't know, older or younger than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: There were persons who were unshaven, with moustaches, and beards. Is that correct? Among them, I mean.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, there were such people, but it was not asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And among those wearing green uniforms, you didn't see any insignia or emblems. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They didn't wear caps either. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: On the way, I saw people with hats. I also saw people wearing bandannas, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I mean just the group of 30 persons that I mentioned from the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, but I can't remember this 30 persons, ever mentioning it in my statement. I can't remember how many there were on the street or on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You did mention around 30 members, but it's not necessary to clarify that in particular. You also mentioned today that you mentioned two Pinzgauer vehicles.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You said one was blue and the other was camouflage colours. On those vehicles you did not see any signs - isn't that correct - that were at the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not see any insignia, but the ones wearing blue were policemen. Those in camouflage uniforms, I don't know about them. I didn't write anything about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We seem to be at cross-purposes, Mr. Cepic. Your question is about the vehicles; the answer is about uniforms. And that's because we've leapt from the 30 people to the two Pinzgauers, without perhaps finishing off the question of the 30 individuals that the witness now seems to recollect speaking about. Would it not be worth putting his statement to him to get that clarified?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, you mentioned in your statement, when you reached the secondary school of economics, you encountered a group of 30 individuals, including members of the army, the MUP, the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English statement, it's page 4, paragraph 6. If my learned friends from the Prosecution could help Mr. Konaj locate this paragraph in the Albanian version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you follow me, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Here, in paragraph 6, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Our discussion of a moment ago, did it relate to this part of your statement, the descriptions referred to?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, but you're mixing it up. You said 30 policemen, and so on. But it's true, because at the economic school we were turned back. We were not allowed to go towards Montenegro. Only the ones who had vehicles were allowed to go to Montenegro; the ones on foot were turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So, in conclusion, this description you've given about the age, appearance, and all the details you mention relates to this group of people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, but I was never asked about their ages. This is the first time somebody is asking me about their ages. I couldn't say whether they were 30 or older or younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Could we move to the second point I've embarked upon, relating to the two Pinzgauer vehicles you said you saw at the petrol station on the 27th of March. In your statement it is --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Not at the station. It's the petrol station in the centre of town, when we were expelled from our homes and told to go towards Montenegro. That's where the Pinzgauer was. There was one Pinzgauer and another one that looked like a police tank. The policemen stopped us to go -- they did not allow us to go in the main road, and these were at the police -- sorry, at the petrol station, 10 or 12 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So near those vehicles you saw only policemen.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, no. There were policemen there. There were soldiers on the tank. I couldn't say whether they were soldiers or paramilitaries, I'm not sure. But this one was a police vehicle. It was blue and had very big tires.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, when you say "tank," you mean this armoured jeep. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Well, a tank that has a big gun barrel, and it was camouflage, green/blue camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And it has rubber wheels; right?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I could not see. I did not see whether it had rubber wheels, the ones of the army, or whether it had track chains.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. In your statement in English, page 3, paragraph 4, you said: "We set out on foot to the stone bridge, where we were stopped by two paramilitary soldiers. They had come out from the Stari Most cafe. They were dressed in camouflage uniforms and no caps. When we arrived at the petrol station, there were two Pinzgauers there; one military, another, a police one." That's your statement from 2001. Today, in response to a question from the Prosecutor, you gave us a clarification, saying that one Pinzgauer was blue and the other was green camouflage. You now mention a tank. Could one of the two Pinzgauers have been an armoured jeep? That's what I'm asking, since you are making a confusion.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Please allow me to explain. I did not say "uniforms and masks" -- you -- I said in the statement -- I probably said two Pinzgauers, but one of them was a blue one and then there was this tank, another vehicle, and that was of the army. And they did not wear masks; they had no masks on. Look at the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I am reading your own sentence back to you. You say there were two Pinzgauers. There is no reference to a tank.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was a little different because it had a gun barrel like a cannon barrel; that's why I said it was of the army. I was not a soldier, so I did not know exactly what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, the vehicle you describe as a Pinzgauer, tell us what that looked like, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The police Pinzgauer, a Pinzgauer or a tank, it had big wheels and it was blue, sky colour, dark; while the other one, the tank Pinzgauer, which was of the army, it was green camouflage and had this gun barrel, very long gun barrel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it the Pinzgauer looked like a vehicle and it had a seat for a driver that was obvious to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It had big tires, the police Pinzgauer. It was something that you got in from up -- it's not something that you had a door to go in. It has a turret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is the one without the gun barrel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the one with the gun barrel, how would the driver get into it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From up -- from up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So through -- from the top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw one person, that his body -- you could see his half body from there, and it also had a side door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you have a driving licence?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you are able to drive?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you know how to distinguish between a truck, a passenger car, a bus. Can you distinguish between those; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I believe I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So why are you telling us now something quite different from what you said in 2001? You will agree with me that your memory was much fresher in 2001.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Everything that I said in my statement is true, and I am responsible for everything that I said. And if you find anything, a discrepancy, let me know and I will explain it. As for your questions about the tanks, everybody knows how the tanks look like. They were on TV. What colour they were, what make, everybody could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, we heard quite a different story from you here today, but let us go back to another topic since you seem to have provided clear answers on this. Did you cooperate in any way with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, allow me, please, to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't understand the counsel when he says that we are dealing with a totally different statement. We have the statement before us. I want the counsel to explain why he says it's a different statement. If we are misunderstanding each other, let us explain it, because there's nothing different from what I've said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think I can explain that to you, Mr. Konaj. A Pinzgauer, as we understand it, is a sort of truck that would have side doors for people to go into and it carries a number of military personnel. I don't think, from the evidence we've so far, that you get into a Pinzgauer from the top, which is what you've described. And your statement also makes no reference to either of these vehicles that you describe as a Pinzgauer having a barrel or being a tank. So we're getting a completely different version of the vehicles - that's what counsel is saying - a completely different description of the vehicles today from the one that you appear to have given in the statement. But in the statement, you simply refer to them as Pinzgauers and there may be a misunderstanding in there. So what counsel is trying to do is clarify it, because there's certainly nothing in here to indicate that one of these vehicles might have been a tank.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, then. It is true that, in my statement, I've mentioned two Pinzgauers, and that is because I couldn't tell between different vehicle makes. I was never in the army. I wasn't an expert. The police Pinzgauer had big tires and was blue, while the military one was green camouflage. I haven't described it in detail in the statement because I wasn't asked to do that, but now the counsel asked me to and that's why I explained the details. The second one had the barrel. If I said two Pinzgauers, then it must have been my mistake. But the truth of it is that one was of them was of the police and the other of the military, and they were different colours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Konaj, the one with the barrel, on what did it move? Did it have tracks or wheels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, I really can't remember. I don't know if it was on wheels or tracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the one that you describe as police Pinzgauer, which I think you have told us you would enter from the top, on what basis did you judge that it was the police -- it belonged to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only on the basis of its colour and the fact that a person wearing a blue uniform was on top of it. I haven't mentioned this in my statement because I wasn't asked to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that, but that doesn't prevent counsel from going into the details with you. That's a perfectly proper exercise, and that's why you're here, to clarify these things, so that we are not left in doubt. And just finally, to complete this, the colour of the vehicle that you describe as a police vehicle, remind us of that colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in your evidence earlier today, you described it as green. So, again, we have a measure of confusion --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I always said that the police Pinzgauer was blue. It can't be of any other colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, but I think the evidence recorded early was that it was green. However, let's move on to Mr. Cepic again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, you cannot recall all the details precisely - isn't that correct - when it comes to the vehicles, that is?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. What sort of cooperation did you have with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You didn't have any. Mr. Konaj, you testified in the Milosevic case on the 25th of April, 2002.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that proceeding, in the transcript, page 3792, you said you were familiar with the book by Tahir Zemaj, "Comments about War," where the KLA attack against the village of Lodza is described, and the attack was dated the 5th of July, 1998 and you mentioned that on page 2 of your statement. Are you familiar with this book, indeed?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is true that I said that I heard that Tahir Zemaj's book was published, but not that I had it or that I read it. And Judge May drew his attention to the statement and not to this book, because it was not me who published that book. That book was published by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no more questions for this witness. I suppose that some of my learned friends from the Defence will deal with the Milosevic transcript some more, and that should be 3D129. This is from the Milosevic case, and I would kindly ask that this portion be entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic. I am one of the Defence counsel for Sreten Lukic here today, and I have a number of questions for you. So I would ask you to pay attention to my question so you can give me the most concise and truthful answer possible, since we do have limited time here. Now, first of all, sir, I would like to ask you a question relating to the location of your home within Pec. Could you please tell us where your home was located in 1998 and 19 -- first of all, in 1998, in relation to the centre of Pec and the suburbs of Pec.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In relation to the centre of Peje, it is about 3 kilometres far.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how far is your neighbourhood from the village or suburb of Lodza?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If you go through the main road, the usual road, it's about 5 or 6 kilometres, but as the crow flies, it's about 1 and a half kilometres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how far is your neighbourhood from the so-called JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Approximately about 2 kilometres. They are closer to the town than to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And according to your statement, on the first Saturday of July in 1998, you sent your family to your father's house, which was in the centre of Pec, based upon a premonition of your wife that something bad was going to happen. Am I correct that other Albanian neighbours in your neighbourhood also did likewise; that is to say, they sent family members to spend the night in the centre of Pec rather than in their own neighbourhood, around that same period of time?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: At that time I was almost the only person living there. That part has houses that had been built, but nobody lives in those houses. There are houses that they're using for manufacturing wood and other materials; there are houses where they sell car parts, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And were there any ethnic Serb neighbours in that neighbourhood at that time, in early July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did the neighbourhood that you lived in have a separate name?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: You mean the neighbourhood where I lived? We called it Dardanija 1. Or are you referring to the neighbourhood inhabited by Serbs? It's not clear to me. Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I was asking about the neighbourhood where you live, which I believe you have given an answer to, so I will move on. Now, at 10.30, according to your statement, at 10.30 in the morning following the date when you sent -- when you went to your father's house in the centre of Pec based upon your wife's premonition, you talk about explosions in the direction of Lodza village. Did you at some time, either at that point in time or thereafter, discover that the explosions had been from fierce fighting between the UCK/KLA and Serb forces in Lodza that had caused these explosions?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to the explosions coming from the direction of Lodza village or suburb at 10.30 in the morning, following your departure towards the centre of Pec in July of 1998, did you at that time or at some time thereafter discover that the source of the explosions had been an attack perpetrated by the UCK/KLA against Serb forces in Lodza village?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you've mentioned already, in response to my colleague, the book by Mr. Zemaj. Are you familiar with or have you since that time heard any other pronouncements by Ramush Haradinaj or any other KLA commanders praising the operation in Lodza as one of the most successful operations and attacks conducted by the KLA in the Pec region in 1998?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the Milosevic proceedings, you were asked about your knowledge of your brother's involvement in the KLA; at that time you did not know of it. Since the time of your testimony in the Milosevic proceedings, have you had the opportunity to be enlightened any further about the involvement of your brother in the UCK/KLA movement?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: He hasn't been in Kosova for 16 years. He now received all the paper that allows him to come back to Kosova. He still has not come to Kosova, and you can check this very easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in the Milosevic proceedings, there was discussion about your brother's involvement with fund-raising and organisation of the KLA in Germany. I'm asking you about that. Have you had an opportunity to become further enlightened about your brother's involvement in the KLA since the testimony that you gave in the Milosevic case; if not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could focus just for a brief couple more questions regarding this time period in July of 1998 and the nearby suburb of Lodza. Did you, at any point in time, witness any of the many trenches and fortifications that had been established in and around the Lodza suburb, which was 1 kilometre, as the crow flies, from your home neighbourhood, in July of 1998, or previously?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have occasion to become familiar with the infamous attack that the KLA undertook in Lodza on July the 5th, 1998, wherein a police vehicle was attacked by a hand-held rocket-launcher, resulting in ten wounded casualties among the police and the taking hostage of two policemen, Perovic and Rajkovic, who were then brutally tortured by the KLA, and their dead bodies, which were mutilated, were discovered 40 days after this action, again in 1998?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you know nothing at all about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't know about it then. I hear it here, now. I had to look after my family, my wife, my children, and my mother-in-law, who was 84 years old at that time. I was only concerned to leave for their sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These are events 5 or 6 kilometres by road, and closer as the crow flies, from where you were living, and you heard nothing about them at all until you come here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know about these things then because I was not interested in such things. I've stated in my statement that you could hear gun-fire every now and then; that is true, I've heard gun-fire every now and then. But, as I said, my primary concern was to take my family out of there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It does seem strange, though, that someone living so close to this activity would have no interest in it, which is how you've been translated as describing your position. And that is your position: You're not interested in the conflicts that were taking place at that time between the KLA and the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already said that I didn't hear of that. When the battle of Loxha began, I left my neighbourhood, Dardanija 1, and I went to my father's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, sir, did you follow any of the media reporting of this very dramatic instance, the clash between the KLA and the Serbs and the later discovery of the bodies that had been mutilated, which was widely covered within the local media available in Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I'm not saying that it wasn't talked about; I'm just saying that I was not able to hear about it on TV because I didn't have TV at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The houses were looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a second, sir. I just have two or three more questions dealing with this, and then we'll move on to the looting of houses. Now, your wife's premonition to leave the area the same day as -- just before the attack that we've been discussing in Lodza, was that premonition based on any information from anyone that the KLA was planning such an operation?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I took my two daughters and my mother-in-law to my father's house and remained with my wife only in the house. My wife, just out of fear, simply because of fear, insisted that we left the house as well, and that's why I decided then to leave the house and join the other members of the family at my father's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How far away was your father's place, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three kilometres away, in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take it, then, that since your wife was afraid, she knew about the KLA build-up and the KLA presence in nearby Lodza. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Now you make me suspicious of my own wife, if she knew anything about it or not. But if she knew something, she then might have kept it a secret from me, because she never mentioned it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, did you hear at any point in time, either in 1998 or 1999, about the existence and activities of a KLA detachment of the so-called secret police that operated under the moniker of the Black Arm or the Black Hand in Pec, which was headed by a gentleman named Neto Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Listen, we heard of the KLA, but as for these black police, or whatever you call it, we have not heard, and we haven't heard of Neto Krasniqi either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicate in your statement that in 1999, when you were in the house of your father when NATO began bombing, a certain individual named Bajram Gashi was also present. Do you know if your friend, Bajram Gashi, if he's related to someone named Muharrem Gashi?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood this. Bajram Gashi, when we were expelled, he came, together with six other members of his family, to my father's house because he had been expelled as well, and we stayed together in that house until 7th of July [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, the question that was asked is a rather different question. If you could answer that. Do you know if Bajram Gashi is related to someone called Muharrem Gashi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say yes or no to that because I don't know if they were related.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on, then, to the looting. First of all, are you familiar with the suburb of Brezanik. Is this fairly close to the JNA barracks that we discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: From Berzhanik? Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was asking you about a location, the suburb of Brezanik. I did not ask you about an individual. Are you familiar with the location of the suburb of Brezanik or neighbourhood of Brezanik?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that part is called Berzhanik neighbourhood. I don't know it in detail, because there might be a certain location in Berzhanik that I never visited, despite the fact that I live in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And Brezanik is situated -- now, in reference to your two homes that were damaged and looted in July of 1998, am I correct that you did not personally witness those acts of violence directed against your two homes in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I am not correct or no, you did not witness the damage to your homes being perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not witness the looting, but I have seen them looted afterwards, because a person who worked in the SUP took me and my uncle to the location where the house was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And were you aware of the fact, either at the time or subsequently, since you stayed through July of 1999, that there was a crime spree in Pec and the various suburbs whereby certain individuals were breaking into multiple homes of ethnic Albanians that had been emptied because persons were staying with relatives in the city centre of Pec? Are you familiar of such a crime spree; that is to say, that your home was not the only home that was looted?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, because in October I left. I went to Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you about the fact that -- in August of 1998, were you aware of the fact that the Serbian police in Pec conducted an investigation and arrested an detained several ethnic Serbs, all residents of Pec, all with previous criminal records, who were arrested for this crime spree that spanned from July through August of 1998, for the looting and property damage caused to homes of ethnic Albanians, and that certain personal belongings from these homes were found in the possession of these persons?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about this. I didn't know it then; I don't know now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I mention the names of Celibic Drasko, Minic Milorad, Markovic Dejan, Vlahovic Ranko, all local Serbs from Pec who were detained and arrested for this activity, are any of those names familiar to you as being persons who lived in any of the neighbourhoods surrounding your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't recognise any of the names. But there were Markovics; I raise this surname. But I don't know about the fact whether they looted or robbed and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we could move to 1999. I'd like to focus on the time period where you say you were forced from your, I believe, your father's home. Am I correct that at that time it is your testimony that you were told to go in the direction of Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes. On the 27th of March, we were told to go towards Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at that time, the early days of the NATO bombing, although Serbia and Montenegro were members of the same Yugoslav state, isn't it a fact that people in Pec were talking about the fact that Montenegro would be safe or exempt from NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: What I know is that everybody went there. They were accepted there and sheltered there. But I wasn't allowed to go there because they said, now the numbers are up; nobody else can go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, you previously testified that you were not permitted to go because you did not have a vehicle and that anyone with vehicles was permitted to go. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I'll repeat it again: Everybody who had a vehicle, on Saturday, the 27th of March, and also on the 28th, was allowed to go in that direction. But other people, who were on foot, were not allowed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I can focus your attention to the portion of your statement on, I believe it is, page 3 where you describe or mention a group of several policemen at the cafe Iliriana. Can I first ask you to describe how these policemen were dressed.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: On the 27th of July, when we went in the direction of Montenegro, we saw these seven persons outside the Iliriana cafe. Two or three were seated on the steps. Two had blue uniforms and camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you see any markings or insignia on any of these uniforms of these persons outside the cafe Iliriana?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I swear I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you personally speak with these individuals at that time?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Of course not. They just told us that we had to take side roads, not the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you tell them that you were going to Jarina, which is, in fact, another neighbourhood within Pec city?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, but I was not allowed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that they took no actions to prevent you from going to Jarina, except for advising you to take the side roads?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: We were not allowed to enter Jarina at all. We were told to go in the direction of Rozaje. When I got to the bus station, then I turned and I went to Bajram Dreshaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as far as the bus station is concerned, in your statement, you state that one of the policemen there said, "There is no way for you to go other than to Montenegro." Could you --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you -- could you --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: This was told to us on the 28th. I'm sorry, I said Bajram Dreshaj earlier but I meant Salih Dreshaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Now, I would like to ask you, first of all, about this individual who told you this statement, "There's nowhere for you to go other than Montenegro." How was this gentleman attired?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was a group. On every street or road you could see three or four persons, a policemen, people in camouflage uniforms. One of them told us that we could not go anywhere but to Montenegro. And we followed another person who turned on a side road and went to Salih Dreshaj's house. It was about 4.00 or 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the type of uniform that the individual who told you that you could not go to any place other than to Montenegro, what type of uniform that was, or anything you noticed about the uniform?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I am sorry. There were different kinds of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 28th of March, 1999, when you saw a group of people coming from the area of the Catholic church, as you describe in your statement, you and your family decided to join this group. Am I correct that at that point in time nobody forced you to join this group, did they?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Nobody grabbed my arm and told me to do anything. But when we asked the crowd, "What is going on?" they told us, "They are expelling us from our homes and are telling us to go to Montenegro." And that's when I got my mother-in-law and my mother in a car, while myself, my wife, and two daughters walked and joined the crowd.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, eventually you got to the town centre of Pec, and I would like to ask you a couple of questions relating to that. Now, first of all, could you describe -- you described a gentleman there as a traffic police commander with a megaphone. Do you happen to know the name he person you've identified as a traffic police commander with a megaphone at the town square?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I know him, but I can't remember his name now. He used to live in my father's neighbourhood, behind the mosque. He was a commander of the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how far away from him were you when he made the pronouncement on the megaphone?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: We were in the Peje square. I was at the post office, the same building as the post office today. He was about 20 to 25 metres away, in the centre of the square, because all around him were people from all the neighbourhoods that had come to the centre, from the morning till 11.00 p.m., when I left with the last bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise what type of clothing he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was wearing a civilian uniform, civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that there were quite a few people in the town square such that it was almost impossible to pass along the main road in that area?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Am I correct that, due to the number of persons in the town square at that location and at that time, that it was it was almost impossible to pass along the main road?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No. Everybody was on the pavement, the street leading to Hotel Metohija and then the other one that leads to SUP. Those were empty so that the trucks and the vehicles and the buses would come there and take the population elsewhere. The last batch of buses that came was at 11.00 at night, and there were everywhere policemen and soldiers and also civilians carrying guns that were keeping the streets clear, the main road clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, did you witness anyone else -- did you witness anyone else making pronouncements on the megaphone in the town square, particularly any ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not see any Albanians speaking with a megaphone, just this commander of the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Mr. Konaj, thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Ms. Dragulev.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have a few questions. In light of the confusion regarding vehicles that has arisen today, I would like to show the witness P1325 to help clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I'm going to show you a few photographs of military vehicles, and could you please let us know if any one of those photographs resembles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the Prosecution had a chance to show the pictures of vehicles during examination-in-chief. They did not take that opportunity. I think that now they would be broadening their questioning and opening up new topics; that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't agree. Where there's confusion of this nature and there is a facility available to try to check the matter, as long as the questions put are not leading questions, then there's nothing wrong with following this course of action. So please carry on, Ms. Dragulev.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I will show you three pages of photographs and would ask you to wait with your selection until you've seen all three pages. You described a military tank or a military vehicle earlier on to the Court, and I would like to ask you if any one of those military vehicles resembles the one you described earlier on. Again, please wait until you've seen all pages. I believe this is page 1. And please indicate to the registry once you are ready to move on to page 2.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I'll see the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And there's one more page, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, can we move to page 3?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Please let us know whether you would like to see any of the other pages again.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes. In the first page, photograph number 3 resembles the police Pinzgauer. No, I was wrong. This one here, it's photograph number 2. Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Number 2 resembles which one?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It resembles the police Pinzgauer, blue. I can't discern the colour here, but it resembles that Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And do any of the photographs resemble the military tank that you saw or the other vehicle that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The military tank, this one here resembles it, the one I mentioned, but I'm not sure whether it had track chains or tires. It was number -- it's number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: So did --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I apologise. As I said, the first one resembles the police vehicle because it's metal. But I can't see the colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: So that's number 2, and the other one --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, number 2 resembles the police Pinzgauer. But it was more like a vehicle and here I can see the tires.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And the other vehicle that you saw --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: This one is the army vehicle, while -- as I said, number 2 is the police and number 3, the army one. As I said, this number 2 is similar to the police Pinzgauer but it's not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. The other question I had, Mr. Konaj, was -- you were asked earlier on whether anyone had forced you to leave the house of Mr. Dreshaj, and you mentioned that you had heard that the crowds were being expelled. Did you see anyone being expelled? Did you see any of those expulsions?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: When we got to the door, we could see two or three streets very clearly, and we saw the crowds coming to the direction of Salih Dreshaj's house, where we were. The crowds went towards the economic school and that's where I joined the crowd, and we went to economic school. At that point we were turned back.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: And my last question is actually just a clarification. I think there was a mistake in the transcript, on page 27, line 4, when Mr. Ivetic asked you about the seven policemen that you encountered at cafe Iliriana on the 27th of March. In your response, in the transcript you responded as that having occurred on the 27th of July. I just wanted to clarify that that was either a translation mistake and -- I wanted to ask you whether that was on the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: On the 27th of March and 28th of March we were expelled. It was the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you very much. That was my last question.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: One day before we were expelled, on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, you've mentioned, in your statement and today, your father on a number of occasions. Did he leave Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: My father died in 1990, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are a number of references throughout the statement to your father or your father's house; there's also reference to your uncle. I had formed the impression they were not two separate individuals here, so -- for example, it might be helpful if your have your statement in front of you. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, but what page, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the first page of the statement. It's got the number 2 at the bottom of it in English, the first statement, and it begins with a very short note, interviewer's note, and then there's a paragraph that begins: "My name is Ndrec Konaj." Now, if you go from that paragraph down three paragraphs, you'll see a paragraph beginning: "We went to my uncle's house and there found everyone very upset." You --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is true. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you look at the very last sentence of that paragraph, the very last sentence of that paragraph, and would you read it to me, please.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: On the first page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, read the last sentence of that paragraph that we've just been looking at.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is true. I took my uncle -- I grabbed my uncle by his arm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I grabbed my uncle by his arm, and we left and went back to my father's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So this is the house that belonged to your father, is it?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: May I explain, please? We've got 6 hectares of land there -- I apologise, 6 acres, and there are two houses there, my father's house and my uncle's house. And when the police came, they took my uncle. And when we returned, we went to my father's house, that's true, but it's in the same compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've clarified the position for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. That completes your evidence. Thank you for coming again to the Tribunal to give it. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the simple thing, Mr. Marcussen, if you're taking the next witness, is for us to have our break now and to resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next witness is Mr. Rexhep Krasniqi. He will be testifying about events relevant to paragraph 72(b) of the indictment, the deportation from Prizren municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While the witness walks in, the witness will be a 92 ter witness. He was previously 92 bis (B).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document now placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Krasniqi, we have your statement in front of us, which we have all read, but counsel for the Prosecution and for the accused wish to ask you a number of questions about the statement and about the events that you describe there. The first person to ask these questions will be for the Prosecutor, Mr. Marcussen. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krasniqi. Would you just please confirm your name to the Court. Just say your name.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: My name is Rexhep Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, did you give a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And was that statement given in April 1999, in Albania?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And later on in September, the 19th of September, 2004, did you speak to a number of representatives of the Tribunal again about your statement?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And on that occasion did you have your statement read back to you?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you make some corrections to your statement on that day?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then you were -- were you then asked to sign a declaration?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And before you testified today, was your statement read back to you again, in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you notice that there was a problem with the date indicated on your statement? The statement says it was originally taken on the 12th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. It was a mistake. The statement was taken in April, not in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Apart from that error in the statement, is the statement a correct reflection of what you remembered happening in 1999?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So if you were asked about -- to describe the events you were describing in your statement, you would describe them as they are described in that statement from 1999?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So at this point I would like to tender the witness's statement, which is in the e-court system, as P2378.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, as Judge Bonomy told you and as you know, the Judges and the Defence already have a copy your statement and have read it before they came to court today. They are, therefore, fully aware of what your evidence is in the statement, so I will only have very few questions for you, to clarify a few matters in your statement. First, I would like to ask you whether you have done your military service.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When, approximately, was that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I completely my military service in 1968/1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Secondly, you say in your statement that you live in the village of Dusanov.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where is that compared to Prizren? How far from Prizren is that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: About 2 kilometres, 2, 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dusanov and Prizren, are they separate towns or have they, sort of, merged together so Dusanov is really a suburb to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They are merged together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You explain in your statement that you worked at a factory called Printex, and you explain that you, one morning, noticed that a number of tanks, 50 tanks, were at the factory. To your knowledge, when did the tanks arrive at the factory?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They came on the 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then I have some questions about the events you describe in your statement that took place on the 28th of March, when a number of police and army personnel came to where you live. You have explained in your statement how the police uniforms looked, but I'd like to ask you: The people that are described as being from the army, what kind of clothes were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The people from the army were wearing green uniforms, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And just so it's clear on the record what I'm talking about, I'm talking about the third paragraph on the second page of the statement, and that's the same in all language versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you also say that there were about ten tanks outside, in the street outside your house. Were there only tanks, or were there also other types of vehicles outside your house, in the street?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There were military and police vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If we first deal with the military vehicles, could you describe them in a bit more details. For example, let's start with the cars -- the vehicles you describe as tanks. How did they look?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The military tanks had tracks instead of tires.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was there any kind of weapon mounted on the vehicles you describe as tanks?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. There were 105-millimetre cannons and anti-aircraft weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what colour were the tanks?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: If I could see it, I would be able to describe it; otherwise, I don't know how to describe it. It's a military colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is it greenish or yellow or blue or red or --

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They are not red; they are green.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the other military vehicles you saw, apart from the tanks, do you know what kind of vehicles they were, what they're called?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They are called armoured vehicles, police armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. What colour were they, the armoured vehicles from the police?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, darker in colour than those of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And could you describe the colour. Again, was it darker green? Was it darker -- another colour?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: If I can see them on a photograph, I can describe them in detail, which is which.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, I have an impression at the moment - which may be wrong - that when the witness talks about a tank, he's generally talking about a weapon with a 105-millimetre cannon on it. Now, in the second paragraph on that, the short paragraph on page 2 of the statement, it's as if these were two separate types of artillery. Can we have that clarified? And also whether the reference to "tank" includes anti-aircraft weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, let's go back to what you saw at the factory on the 23rd and deal with that, and then we'll come back to what you saw in your street. Now, on the 23rd, at the factory, you said you saw tanks. Now, apart from the tanks, were there also other weapons?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that there were 105-millimetre artillery pieces. Is that what you're saying, that there were tanks and then artillery pieces at the factory?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you say these different kinds of weapons were military, why is that? What colour were they, for example?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I have completed my military service and I can say that I know these vehicles very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So at the factory, there were tanks and artillery pieces. Now I go back to the events on the 28th of March and the things you saw around your house. You have described to us that you saw tanks, which were vehicles running on tracks, that had a cannon on them. Were there also artillery in your street, or was that only at the factory?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We are talking only about the 23rd at the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were there military vehicles in your street which had anti-aircraft guns on them?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm not clear. Are you referring to the 23rd or the 28th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: On the 28th, sorry.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: On the 28th, the tanks were the same in colour as those at the factory, with the exception of the police APCs; they were different in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you also saw different kinds of equipment outside your house, that you saw tanks and then police APCs. Are you able to describe the colour of the APCs to the Court?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The colour was darker than the military colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was the colour similar to some of those colours found on the police camouflage uniforms that you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it resembles that colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Apart from the tanks and the APCs, were there other kinds of vehicles, or were there tanks and APCs only?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Only tanks and APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to clarify another point in your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- does that mean that there's some mistake along the way in referring to anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, did you, at any stage this morning, talk about anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since they were there, I could see that, and there were anti-aircraft pieces, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, the anti-aircraft vehicles, where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Those were on the top of the tank, on the front side of the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So the tank, apart from having a cannon, also had an anti-aircraft gun on them; is that how you describe it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That anti-aircraft gun, can you describe how it looked?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They have a barrel, a thinner barrel, on the top of the tank, on the front side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: From the -- why do you say they are anti-aircraft weapons? Is there anything in particular that makes you think they were anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: As I said, I have completed my military service and I can tell between anti-aircraft and anti-personnel weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if you could explain to us what the main difference is, then that will be helpful, please.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The 105-millimetre cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe my question was unclear. The gun that was an anti-aircraft gun, why do you say that is different from the gun you describe as an anti-personnel gun?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It is because the anti-aircraft, the surface-to-air, is on the top, while the surface-to-surface, they have it on the front side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we will leave the evidence as it is on the record now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something else about what happened on the 28th, in the morning. You describe how the police came into your house or the area where you lived and you had some other people in your house that had come there before. Was anybody forced to pay money to the people who came into your house?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was anybody beaten?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I want to be clear on this. It's not clear to me. Can you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the morning, when you were expelled from your house, were people beaten at your house?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They beat all of them, including my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anybody need treatment afterwards because they had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who did?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, members of my family, as well as other people needed treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anyone have to be attended to at a hospital?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, we didn't take them to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anyone go to the hospital later on because they had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: We didn't go to the hospital there, but we visited one in Kruja and Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who was taken to the hospital in Kruja and Tirana?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: My son's daughter, who was only 8 months old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How long did she have to stay in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Eight days, while my brother, in Tirana, 17 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the transcript, when I asked you who had to go to the daughter, you said your son's daughter. Now I understand that there was also another person, namely your brother, who had to be hospitalised. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, I have two short points more to clarify with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you do that ... What treatment did your granddaughter require?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the police forces entered my house, they grabbed her by her neck and they made some injuries on her neck and her chest. So we went to Albania, we took her to the hospital. There was no way that we could take her to the hospital in our area because they came there to massacre us, not to give us any treatment. The Serb police forces came to my house. They grabbed my granddaughter by her neck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you listen to my question, please. What treatment did she require in Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They first treated her wound on the -- the injuries, because she was scratched on her neck, and then again another treatment for the other damages that she suffered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what treatment did your brother require?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in Tirana; we were in Kruja. I went to visit him at the hospital after five or six days. It was impossible for us to meet before. When we arrived in Albania, we actually lost contact between each other. I went to visit him later.
